newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK VSZ STILL TO DECIDE ON CZECH SKODA STAKE.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK VSZ STILL TO DECIDE ON CZECH SKODA STAKE.

text.p: Slovak steel maker VSZ a.s. said on Tuesday it was still to decide about the possibility of acquiring an undisclosed stake in Czech engineering concern Skoda a.s. .

In a statement issued after a meeting of its board of directors, VSZ said it had not declared an interest in buying an 8.7 percent stake in Skoda from the Czech government privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF).

"The VSZ board of directors has not declared an interest in buying the 8.7 percent stake of Skoda Plzen if available. The truth is that some preliminary unbinding talks on this topic had happened," the statement said.
It added that the results of the talks were being assessed by its specialists, and that VSZ management would decide about the issue after a "careful consideration".
But it was not clear whether the topic and talks exclusively referred to the 8.7 percent recently chosen by the NPF for sale, nor with whom the talks had been held.
On Monday, VSZ spokesman Jozef Marko told Reuters that VSZ had declared an "interest in Skoda" and that certain "probing" negotiations were ongoing about whether it would get an undisclosed stake.

Two of Skoda's major shareholders, banks IPB and Komercni Banka -- which hold 5.9 percent and 11.7 percent of Skoda respectively -- both declined comment on Monday as to whether they were in talks with VSZ on selling their stakes.
The Czech NPF said last Wednesday it was planning to sell the 8.7 percent stake it holds in Skoda soon.
Skoda's largest shareholder is NERo s.r.o., owned by Skoda General Director Lubomir Soudek. He has expressed an interest in adding the NPF stake to his current 21.5 percent holding in Skoda.
The company is the largest Czech engineering concern, based in the western city of Plzen. Skoda's production ranges from beer cans to trucks and nuclear reactors.
It is no longer affiliated with Volkswagen AG's Czech unit, car maker Skoda Automobilova a.s. .
VSZ is Slovakia's largest steel maker, employing some 25,000 workers. It has some 100 subsidiaries and holds stakes in firms ranging from banks to airlines to soccer teams.
